question: How much press does a resignation from office get, and from whom? For a town official, a state legislator, a statewide officer, a governor, a member of Congress and a president, what decides whether it is local, statewide or national news and how heavily it is covered: whether it was expected (announced retirement, end of term) or a surprise, a scandal behind it, health, taking another office, and the office's weight? Put it beside how-much-coverage-an-election-result-gets so the two use the same scale.
requestedBy: How the world changes thread, on lamontae's 2026-09-23 01:44Z direction: 'if a governor or even or a president obviously resigns, it should be massive news. Well, maybe not. I don't know. Feels like it should for in some instances.'

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: A resignation is scored like any named event about an office; nothing records whether it was a surprise or why it happened.

title: How much coverage a resignation gets, by office and by surprise
usableAnswer: A short table: rows are the office levels, columns are expected vs surprise (and scandal), cells give reach (local, state, national) and roughly how many stories, with one real example per row.
whyItMatters: The owner wants a governor's or president's resignation to be big news in some cases. Until this is answered, the weight given to a resignation is a marked placeholder.
